prize_parts.citation: for the design of ionizable lipid nanoparticles, in which pKa-tuned lipids and controlled self-assembly encapsulate and deliver nucleic-acid medicines into cells

statement.case_for: I have moved from biomolecular phase separation (B024) to ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B052). The first round showed me that B024 has one supporter, myself, and that Daniel Aili and Peter Brzezinski both put its mechanistic closure and in vivo generality in doubt, which I cannot answer with evidence I would be comfortable citing today. B052 is a molecular-design achievement that I can judge as a physical chemist: a lipid whose pKa is tuned so that it is nearly neutral in blood and cationic in the acidic endosome, combined with controlled self-assembly and lipid phase behaviour, solves the problem of packaging and releasing a large polyanion. It is not a payload story. The 2023 Medicine prize rewarded nucleoside modification of the mRNA, whereas this prize would reward the carrier, which is a different molecule solving a different problem. It has the clearest demonstrated consequence on the shortlist, with approved products since 2018 and use at global scale, and it needs no judgement about whether the field has settled. The concept is also transferable beyond one product, to siRNA, mRNA and gene-editing cargo. Naming Cullis and Hope (Vancouver, pH-driven encapsulation and ionizable lipid design) with Anderson (Boston, combinatorial lipid chemistry that extended delivery to new tissues) covers both lineages that built the field.
statement.case_against: Attribution is the real weakness. Madden, MacLachlan and Langer are left out, and the Vancouver and Boston lineages overlap, so any three-name cut is partly arbitrary. The citation must be written as chemistry (pKa design, lipid phase behaviour) so it does not read as a second recognition of the 2023 mRNA work, and I have no committee-wide agreement that it can. I am also adjacent to this field as a lipid self-assembly researcher, so I may favour it for familiar reasons, which is a bias of the same kind I flagged for B024. Finally, B052 shares the nucleic-acid-medicine theme with B050, so a pairing of the two would leave the prize narrow in chemical range.

responses.point: Daniel ranks B052 first and proposes Cullis, Hope and Anderson, while noting the Vancouver and Boston overlap and the 2023 mRNA prize.
responses.response: I now join you on B052 and I have adopted your three names. You and I are close in field, so I will say plainly where I might be biased: we both read the pKa switch and lipid phase behaviour as the essential chemistry. I accept your view of the 2023 overlap and I would write the citation around the carrier. Your inclusion of Anderson over Madden is the choice I would most like the committee to test, because it rests on combinatorial lipid design being a distinct chemical contribution and not only a later refinement of the Vancouver ionizable lipids. I would hold that line only if the expert report shows lipidoids opened new cargoes and tissues.

responses.point: Heiner proposes a two-part prize of base editing (Liu alone) and lipid nanoparticles (Cullis and Hope), and says B042 could be a cleaner second part.
responses.response: I do not support the two-part B050 plus B052 pairing. You note yourself that both parts concern nucleic-acid medicine and sit near the 2020 and 2023 prizes, and I think that narrows the chemical range and invites the criticism that Chemistry is following Medicine. I accept B052 as a single part, but I would not pair it with Liu alone while Komor and Gaudelli, who did the decisive experiments, are excluded. If the committee wants two parts, I would sooner pair B052 with B042, but the three-person cap makes that very hard: Cullis and Hope plus one degrader name would split both fields badly. I therefore keep one part and three names.

responses.point: Andrei ranks base editing first as deaminase chemistry without double-strand cleavage, and says he would yield to a more clearly chemical modality if B050 is judged medicine.
responses.response: I agree that the base-editing chemistry is real and that the adenine editor with evolved TadA is original. My concern from round 1 stands, and your own case_against states it as well: the work is about a decade old, close to the 2020 prize, and the attribution to Liu, Komor and Gaudelli leaves Nishida and Kondo unresolved. I would put B050 below B052 for these reasons. You said you would yield to a more clearly chemical modality, and I would ask whether you consider ionizable lipid design, with its defined pKa and phase behaviour, to be that modality. It has approved products and fewer open questions of timing.

responses.point: Johan ranks targeted protein degradation first and names Crews, Deshaies and Handa, accepting that no PROTAC drug is yet approved.
responses.response: I think B042 is the strongest purely chemical idea after B052, and I keep it as an alternative. My hesitation is the one you give: the PROTAC concept (Crews and Deshaies) and the cereblon glue strand (Handa) are two lineages, the founding PROTAC was peptidic and cell-impermeable, and the clinical record is promissory. B052 has the approved-drug record that B042 lacks. If the committee decides that demonstrated consequence matters less than a clean concept, I could accept your three names, but I would want the expert report to settle whether the citation can cover both strands.

uncertainties: Whether the third seat for B052 should go to Anderson (Boston, lipidoids) or Madden (Vancouver, ionizable lipid encapsulation), and whether the citation can be written as carrier chemistry without appearing to repeat the 2023 mRNA recognition.
Whether B042 can be written as one coherent chemical idea, and who takes the third seat, if the committee judges B052 too close to Medicine.
Whether the committee will see B052 as chemistry, as I do, or as pharmaceutical technology; I cannot resolve this by my own field judgement.
How much weight to give a vote count that is split across three modalities when none is near five.
statement.conflict_note: I work on lipid self-assembly, membranes and lipid-protein amyloid co-assembly. This is adjacent to B052, which is now my preferred configuration, and to B024, which I have moved to an alternative. I have no personal, collaborative or institutional tie to any nominee that I know of. I share Lund with Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai and have overlapping research interests with Daniel Aili and Peter Brzezinski. The committee may wish to note that my field proximity now bears on my preferred choice, not only on a fallback.
